vackyPlanArtifact.title: Travel Memory And Traveler Profile Epic Implementation Plan

summary.paragraph: This ships a memory-capable trip mode, validated trip and location memory signals, a deterministic read-time traveler profile, user confirmation/correction of profile variables, and a frozen profile contract for the later AI-assisted planner; it defers AI/LLM calls, embeddings, vector search, photo flows, graph JSON, snapshot tables, background jobs, hosted database assumptions, and any planner runtime. At the end, the planner feature receives a versioned `travelerProfile.v1` JSON contract plus a Lisbon dry-run context bundle proving the contract is sufficient for a future planning request.

chosenDefaults.default: Use `tripMode: optional string` on `Trip`, with new writes setting `PLANNED` or `COMPLETED` explicitly and legacy missing values normalized to `PLANNED` on read.
Only explicit `tripMode == COMPLETED` rows feed `/memories` and profile computation; date-derived past/upcoming remains display flavor only.
Store per-trip companions as `companionsJson: optional string`, a JSON array of controlled companion enum values, because one trip can include more than one context.
Use `memoryTagsJson` for optional stop-level controlled style/category tags; raw free text remains in `memorySummary` and existing location `notes` only.
Persist only explicit user profile confirmations/overrides in a user-scoped override table; do not persist computed profile snapshots.

Phase 2 introduces a narrowly scoped deterministic profile test command; Vitest is the preferred minimal TS test runner, but the task is flagged as a tooling decision because the repo currently has no test runner.

keyChanges.change: Add optional/defaulted memory columns to `trip` and `location`; update generated bindings only through `npm run stdb:generate`.
Add server actions that all call `requireSession()` before reducer calls.
Add `/memories` as a server-rendered profile and completed-memory surface, with client islands only for correction/confirmation forms.
Add a pure `computeTravelerProfile(rows, filters)` engine in `lib/traveler-profile/` with deterministic sorting, confidence, sample size, slice filters, and zero external calls.
Freeze the profile contract in `brain/wiki/architecture/traveler-profile-contract.md` and a Phase 3 decision record before planner work starts.

interfacesAndDataRules.rule: Free text is stored raw in `Trip.memorySummary` and `Location.notes`; no reducer or profile function distills it into structured fields.
Profile computation reads only stored SpacetimeDB rows returned through safe server reads; it performs no Google, UploadThing, OpenAI, LLM, embedding, vector, or graphify runtime calls.
Every profile variable must include `value`, `confidence`, and `sampleSize`; Phase 3 adds `provenance` without removing those fields.
Stable JSON means stable object key insertion order in builders and stable array sorting by score descending, then key/title ascending, then id ascending.
Profile overrides apply after derived computation and never mutate source Trip or Location memory rows.

phase0.scope: Close RISK-010 by recording memory-first as an accepted product direction before any schema, reducer, UI, or profile implementation begins.

decisionRecord.content:
# Memory-First Travel Memory And Traveler Profile
## Decided
Vacky accepts memory-first as a product direction for the Travel Memory and Traveler Profile epic. The app will treat completed trips as a structured behavioral dataset that can later feed AI-assisted planning. The accepted v1 path is explicit completed-trip memory capture, deterministic profile derivation from relational rows, and a user-confirmed profile contract. The planner remains a separate later feature.
## Options Considered
1. Stay planning-first only and defer completed-trip memory capture. 2. Add a lightweight past-trip memories module without making it a durable product direction. 3. Accept memory-first now and build completed-trip memory capture plus a deterministic traveler profile before planner work. 4. Jump directly to AI-assisted planning and let the AI infer profile preferences from notes.
## Why This Option Won
Option 3 wins because the planner needs trusted input before it can produce useful recommendations. Completed trips provide revealed preference: what the user actually visited, liked, repeated, and would skip. A deterministic profile gives the future planner a stable interface with confidence and sample size, instead of making an LLM rediscover preferences differently on every request. Keeping the source of truth relational also avoids snapshot, vector, and graph persistence before the app has enough data volume to justify it.
## Accepted Downsides
- Old trips need exact dates before they can become completed memories. Existing date-derived past trips do not automatically enter the profile; the user must explicitly convert each one to `COMPLETED`. - V1 is photo-less. `imagesJson` remains a known reserved schema surface, but this epic deliberately excludes photo flows and does not use photos as profile evidence. - Manual reconstruction has friction. Users may need to enter old stops, verdicts, notes, pace, and companions after the fact. - The first profile will be sparse for cold-start users. The UI must show low confidence at 0 or 1 completed trips instead of pretending certainty. - The profile is computed on read. This is acceptable while per-user data is expected to remain in dozens of trips and hundreds of stops, but it should be revisited if latency becomes visible.
## Revisit Criteria
Revisit this decision if:
- User testing shows completed-trip reconstruction is not adopted even when past-dated planned trips have a visible convert-to-memory path. - Planner dry runs in Phase 3 cannot answer realistic planning requests without adding photos, external enrichment, embeddings, graph persistence, or snapshot tables. - Profile computation becomes measurably slow on realistic local datasets. - The product shifts back to booking-first or live-trip execution as the primary strategy. - A later AI planner spec needs contract fields that cannot be derived from the relational memory dataset without violating the no-AI/no-external-call constraints of this epic.

reducer.name: create_trip
reducer.parameters: userId: u64, title: string, description: string, coverImageUrl?: string, startDate: timestamp, endDate: timestamp, tripMode?: string
reducer.validation: Existing user must exist; title/description/date validation remains; `tripMode` must be omitted, `PLANNED`, or `COMPLETED`; omitted writes `PLANNED`.
reducer.ownership: Creation validates `userId` exists; no `requireOwnedTrip` is applicable before the trip exists.

reducer.name: set_trip_mode
reducer.parameters: userId: u64, tripId: u64, tripMode: string
reducer.transitionSemantics: Allows `PLANNED` to `COMPLETED` and `COMPLETED` to `PLANNED`. Reverting to `PLANNED` preserves `memorySummary`, `overallAppreciation`, `travelStyleTagsJson`, `pace`, `companionsJson`, `memoryVerdict`, and `memoryTagsJson`, but profile reads ignore the trip until it is set back to `COMPLETED`.

reducer.name: save_trip_memory
reducer.parameters: userId: u64, tripId: u64, memorySummary?: string, overallAppreciation?: i32, travelStyleTags: string[], pace?: string, companions: string[]
reducer.validation: `overallAppreciation` must be 1-5 when provided; `travelStyleTags`, `pace`, and `companions` must match controlled vocabularies; arrays are deduped and stable-sorted before JSON storage; free text is only trimmed, not distilled.

reducer.name: save_location_memory
reducer.parameters: userId: u64, tripId: u64, locationId: u64, memoryVerdict?: string, memoryTags: string[], appreciation?: i32, priceSentiment?: string, notes?: string
reducer.validation: `memoryVerdict` must be omitted or one of `FAVORITE`, `LIKED`, `NEUTRAL`, `SKIP_NEXT_TIME`; `memoryTags` must match controlled tags; `appreciation` remains optional 1-5 detail; `priceSentiment` must reuse existing `LOCATION_PRICE_SENTIMENTS`; `notes` remains raw text.
reducer.ownership: Calls `requireOwnedTrip(ctx.db, userId, tripId)`, then verifies `locationId` exists and belongs to `tripId`.

task.acceptanceCriteria: Invalid enum/tag payloads are rejected inside reducers even if a hostile client bypasses UI and server-action validation. `SKIP_NEXT_TIME` is stored, not discarded. No reducer writes snapshot, graph, AI, photo, or external-service data.

Request `/memories` unauthenticated; expected result: no derived or confirmed profile data is readable.

Search implementation for `fetch`, OpenAI, embeddings, vector DB, background job, graph JSON, snapshot table, UploadThing photo flow, Maincloud, Neon, or hosted Postgres additions; expected result: none introduced.

regression.checkpoint: Phase 1 capture flows still work after overrides exist: create completed trip, save trip memory, save location memory, revert mode.
Phase 2 derived-only profile behavior still works when no overrides exist.
Existing planned-trip flows, itinerary create/edit/reorder, globe, and dashboard tabs remain unaffected.

rollback.step: If override table/reducers fail, revert Phase 3 schema/module/action/UI files and republish/regenerate back to the Phase 2 module. Keep the Phase 2 derived profile shipped.

If contract freeze or dry run exposes missing profile fields, do not expand implementation silently; record the gap in `risksAndOpenQuestions` and either amend Phase 3 tasks before merge or create a new decision record.
If local SpacetimeDB cannot remove an already-published override table non-destructively, stop and request explicit approval before any local-only reset.

confidenceFunction.rule: For each contributing trip, recency weight is 1.0 when `asOfDate - trip.endDate <= 365 days`, 0.7 when 366-1095 days, and 0.4 when older than 1095 days.

Effective sample size is the sum of recency weights over the unit relevant to the variable: trips for trip-level variables, locations for location-level variables, and notes for evidence-backed variables.
Base confidence score is `min(1, effectiveSampleSize / 10)` for location-level variables and `min(1, effectiveSampleSize / 5)` for trip-level variables.
Cold-start cap: if completedTripCount is 0, score is 0; if completedTripCount is 1, score is capped at 0.34 even with many stops.
Confidence label is `low` for score < 0.35, `medium` for score >= 0.35 and < 0.75, and `high` for score >= 0.75.
Scores are rounded to two decimals after all weighting and caps, using deterministic numeric rounding.

sliceFilters.filter: When present, include trips whose `companionsJson` intersects the requested companion list. Empty or missing filter includes all completed trips.
When present, include trips whose `endDate` is within that many days of `asOfDate`; then still apply recency weights inside the included set.
Required for deterministic computation and tests; UI may pass today's date from the server.

provenance.marker: The value came only from completed trip/location rows and deterministic computation.
The value came from a user override/confirmation row; confidence and sampleSize still reflect the underlying evidence base unless the contract is changed by decision record.

evidenceSelectionRule.rule: Select raw trip `memorySummary` for the three most recent completed trips in the active slice when present.
Select location `notes` for up to five `FAVORITE` locations and up to five `SKIP_NEXT_TIME` locations in the active slice.
Sort evidence by reason priority: confirmed-variable-support, skip, favorite, recent; then by trip end date descending; then location order ascending; then id ascending.
Do not summarize, rewrite, classify, or pre-distill notes. Pass raw text with source ids and reason metadata only.

plannerDryRun.request: 5 days in Lisbon with my partner
plannerDryRun.deliverable: The brief must include a context bundle with `filters.companions = ["COUPLE"]`, a realistic sliced `travelerProfile.v1` object, selected raw favorite/skip/recent notes, and a short sufficiency analysis proving the planner can decide pace, category balance, price posture, likely exclusions, and what to ask the user next without reopening this epic.
plannerDryRun.example:
Planning request: "5 days in Lisbon with my partner"
Context bundle: - profileVersion: travelerProfile.v1 - filters: { companions: ["COUPLE"], recencyWindowDays: null, asOfDate: "2026-06-12" } - variables.categoryAffinity: confirmed or derived top categories, each with value/confidence/sampleSize - variables.behavioralPace: stops-per-day preference with confidence/sampleSize - variables.priceSentiment: preferred cost feel with confidence/sampleSize - variables.skipPatterns: explicit SKIP_NEXT_TIME categories/tags/place types - evidence.selectedRawNotes: raw notes from FAVORITE and SKIP_NEXT_TIME stops, not summarized
Sufficiency proof: - Planner can bias toward high-confidence favorites. - Planner can avoid skip patterns even when sparse because negative signals are first-class. - Planner can distinguish couple-trip evidence from solo/family/work history. - Planner can ask follow-up questions for low-confidence variables instead of hallucinating certainty.

existingRiskInteractions.risk: Profile reads must not call `/api/trips` reverse geocoding or any Google APIs. Phase 2 hostile checks inspect for external calls.
Each phase extends verification scope with explicit hostile-client checks for new reducers, actions, unauthenticated reads, and cross-user access.
`imagesJson` remains accepted/reserved and unused. This epic deliberately excludes photo flows even though memories may later want photos.

newRisks.risk: Profile override rows are user-level, not trip-owned, so `requireOwnedTrip` cannot literally authorize them. Mitigation: server actions derive `userId` from `requireSession()`, reducers/procedures scope by `userId`, and Reviewer must explicitly accept this exception or require a revised ownership model before Phase 3.

Adding Vitest for one deterministic pure-function test introduces new dev tooling. Mitigation: decide before Phase 2 starts; keep the script narrowly scoped or use a documented no-dependency alternative.

SpacetimeDB optional-column publishes are intended non-destructive, but local schema evolution has no migration safety net. Mitigation: run publish before app imports change, keep rollback explicit, and require user approval for any local reset.

openQuestions.question: HR-13 says every new mutating reducer must enforce ownership via `requireOwnedTrip`, but profile overrides are user-level and have no trip id. Phase 3 should either accept the session-user scoped override reducer exception or revise the epic to require a different ownership primitive for user-owned rows.

The exact controlled style tag set is chosen from the superseded 2026-06-11 plan because the accepted epic names style tags but does not enumerate them. If product wants fewer tags, change them before Phase 1 schema/reducer work starts.
Vitest is the cleanest deterministic TypeScript test path, but adding it is a tooling decision. If rejected, Phase 2 must still provide an executable byte-identical profile JSON check.

estimates.phaseEstimate: Riskiest task: getting the decision wording accepted without weakening the epic. Mitigation: use the drafted content verbatim and review RISK-010 before merge.
Riskiest task: schema/reducer changes plus generated bindings. Mitigation: publish/generate before app imports, keep columns optional/default-on-read, and hostile-test invalid vocab writes.
Riskiest task: deterministic profile computation and test tooling. Mitigation: stable sorting/stringification, fixed `asOfDate`, and a small dedicated determinism command.

Riskiest task: user-level override authorization and contract freeze. Mitigation: require Reviewer acceptance of the user-scope guard, document the HR-13 exception, and do not freeze the contract until the Lisbon dry run passes.
